messages.content: Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6.

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.content:
**Standard error of the sample mean (under the null)**  

The “standard deviation of the null‑hypothesis test” is usually interpreted as the standard error of the sampling distribution of the sample mean when the null hypothesis is true.  
It is calculated as:

\[
SE = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}}
\]

where  
- \(s = 1.4\) (sample standard deviation)  
- \(n = 40\) (sample size)

\[
SE = \frac{1.4}{\sqrt{40}} \approx \frac{1.4}{6.3249} \approx 0.221
\]

So the standard deviation (standard error) of the null‑hypothesis test is **≈ 0.22**.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6."

They want the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test? That likely refers to the standard error of the mean under null hypothesis? The standard error = sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size). But they mention population mean 98.6. The standard deviation of the null hypothesis test might be the standard error of the sampling distribution of the sample mean under null. That is sigma/sqrt(n). So compute 1.4 / sqrt(40). sqrt(40) ≈ 6.3249. 1.4 / 6.3249 ≈ 0.2213. So about 0.221.

Alternatively, maybe they want the standard deviation of the test statistic? For t-test, the standard deviation of the t distribution is sqrt((n-1)/(n-3))? But likely they want standard error.

Thus answer: approx 0.221. Provide explanation.
